units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 3:1:2">Y. Yoma III, beg. 40ᵇ</cite>; Y. R. Hash. II, beg. 57ᵈ what is <cite ref="B00389"><he>בורקי</he></cite> (Mish.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 3:1">Yoma III, 1</cite>)? It means <cite ref="B01331"><he>בָּרֶקֶת</he></cite>, the rising light, as people say in Babylonia (<he>בְּרַק ברוקא</he>) <he>בְּרוּק ברוקה</he> the sparkling (star) shines, meaning <he>אנהר מנהורא</he> the light-giver (morning star) gives light. [Bab.

<cite ref="Yoma 28b:1">Yoma 28ᵇ</cite> (hebr.) <he>בָּרַק ברקאי</he>.] <cite ref="Berakhot 59a:7">Ber. 59ᵃ</cite> (expl. <he>רעמים</he>) <he>ברקא תקיפא דבריק בעננא וכ׳</he> an intense lightning which flashes through the cloud and breaks pieces of hailstone, (Var. v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.).

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 144:6">Targ. Ps. CXLIV, 6</cite>.—Targ. II Esth. III, 8 <he>מבריקין עיניהון</he> their eyes sparkling (in defiance). [<cite ref="Chullin 112a">Ḥull. 112ᵃ</cite> <he>דאבריק</he> some ed., read <he>דאבריה</he>, v. <cite ref="B01154"><he>בְּרָא</he></cite>.]
